Preserve the room’s five zones and the six project destinations. Within Studio, Converse, Explore and Build show the same project through different local lenses; source, discussions, decisions and admitted work remain connected.

Keep what already works

  • Luis’s quiet violet atmosphere and expressive Sophia presence.
  • The persistent conversation dock and useful entry routes.

Five zones, one working context

The header establishes who is here, the current audience and the shared focus. The central stage holds the current conversation or artifact. Discussion stays beside its exact target. Sophia’s dock remains available. An optional inspector reveals source, versions, checks and consequences without shrinking the artifact into a thumbnail.

Let the work take the stage

Converse gives active discussion and a concise “Where we stand” summary room to breathe. Explore brings directions, research and experiments forward. Build emphasizes the selected creation and its coherent preview. These are local views of one project, not separate conversations or mandatory stages.

The journey to demonstrate

Enter, discuss, make the idea visible, browse independently, request and pass shared control, revise a precise target, agree a direction and inspect its handoff. Then review partial work, answer an owner request, amend within scope, keep larger changes as follow-up, recover the same execution, inspect failed and corrected evidence, accept and return.

Every change has a place in the workspace

The button below each change instruction opens a focused example of that exact behavior. Numbered annotations identify the relevant zone. After inspecting it, return to the prior walkthrough with its actor, source, draft, work and obligations preserved.

Visible completion: A reader can identify the project, people, local lens, shared focus, artifact, Sophia and active work, then follow a change instruction into its exact workspace example.

Retain personal entry routes and project-led team entry. A local lens changes the view, not the audience. Opening the project restores its actual sources, discussions, accepted results and pending work without creating another execution.

Keep what already works

  • Personal goals, journal, rituals, and memory remain useful.
  • The cross-project board remains an overview, with its List and Board alternatives.

Scope changes the audience

Personal / Team updates navigation, composer context, Updates, and available knowledge together. A private draft stays in its original scope; it is never copied into the shared composer automatically.

A room belongs to a project

Home and an Activity item open the same project. Studio / Conversations / Goals / Work / Knowledge / Activity remain the project destinations. Converse / Explore / Build sit inside Studio. Moving among them changes local composition while preserving project and artifact identity.

Leave without losing the project

Leaving a room does not close the project or cancel accepted work. On return, show accepted changes, outstanding follow-ups, current owner actions and the last known execution state. Reading a notification does not remove an unresolved request from this return view.

Start in the lens that fits

Converse can begin with an emerging idea; Explore can begin with a question or reference; empty Build offers a first creation or existing source. A clear mandate may start a build directly. Neither a repository connection nor a previously agreed mockup is a universal entry requirement.

Return to the same obligation

If the development connection still needs Luis, the same H1 appears in the project return, Goals, Work and the Studio bridge. It names the affected database dependency. Independent work may continue only while its own executor state permits it.

Visible completion: Switching scope retains private drafts; changing lens retains shared work; returning still shows H1 until its owner action and continuation are resolved.

Keep first-artifact creation, targeted v3-to-v4 revision, old comments and technical diagrams. Add two design directions and a runnable frontend whose local interaction is real while its services are explicitly simulated.

Keep what already works

  • Conversation, Explore, and Build remain useful ways of working.
  • Free browsing remains available alongside deliberate shared focus.

An empty state should begin the work

Offer Make a first mockup, Explore the technical approach, Bring an artifact and direct creation in Build. Each opens meaningful local material through a deliberate action. This offline file makes no upload, paid image generation or model-response claim.

A visible, bounded revision

Preserve the original welcome-panel co-review: v3 has competing actions; v4 establishes one primary action while keeping the header and visual identity. Its comments remain on their original version. Open the old target, compare, or create an explicitly linked follow-up rather than rewriting its past.

Ideas beyond mockups

The technical example still challenges a client-only coordination assumption, revises the control diagram and opens its sourced rationale and bounded brief. External surface takeover remains a labeled extension, distinct from a person handing the shared guide role to another person.

Compare directions with equivalent content

Direction A uses editorial clarity: typography and reading rhythm. Direction B uses a warmer product invitation and an approved illustration. Compare the same welcome content and core action at desktop and narrow sizes. Selecting a direction pins its reference; it does not discard alternatives or start an executor.

Keep the asset and the source

The selected artwork carries an identity, version, provenance, crop intent and permitted role. A copy edit preserves it. A failed replacement leaves the approved asset intact. The prototype and handoff use shared frontend source, tokens, assets and behavior definitions, rather than rebuilding the interface from a screenshot.

Try the frontend; inspect the boundary

Open the main action, inspect project content, and try loading, empty, error, long-content and permission-refused states. The local controls genuinely respond; identity, services, persistence and delivery to another participant are simulated. Purpose and maturity remain separate: an executable experiment may still belong in Explore.

A website can begin without a repository

A secondary path is saved in Sophia before GitHub is connected. Inspect or download its actual source, styles and assets. A later external revision requires reconciliation; exporting source, synchronizing, merging and publishing remain different actions.

Visible completion: Both directions use equivalent content; the selected welcome component responds locally; an edit preserves the header, original comments, source lineage and approved asset.

“The direction stays with the project.”

Ready to hand overAgree a direction before implementation.
Ready when calledTeam Sophia · Meaningful decisions

Retain request, grant, decline, return, reclaim and stale-control handling. Davide owns final product acceptance; Luis owns the development connection. Either may make an allowed welcome-flow amendment, independently of the guide role.

Keep what already works

  • Local browsing does not retask background work.
  • Human discussion remains central; one Sophia participates in the room.

Make the handoff lightweight

Luis can browse a reference locally while Davide guides. Request control creates a visible pending request; the host grants or declines it. After transfer, a stale former-guide action is rejected rather than quietly changing shared focus.

Quiet until clearly invited

Invoke Sophia illustrates the wake phrase without using a microphone. Follow-ups remain within one bounded exchange, then Sophia returns to Ready when called. Microphone availability, context listening, recording, and memory are separate concepts.

Keep boundaries legible

Guide transfer changes shared-focus authority only. Davide remains responsible for final product acceptance; Luis retains the development connection. Both have a bounded welcome-flow design grant. If the host is offline without a deputy, shared-control transfer waits while permitted discussion and local reading remain available.

One conversation, several useful entry points

Keep Conversations as the project archive beside Studio. Converse and the canvas thread show those same messages in context. Search by project, goal, work, artifact, author and unresolved status. Each entry retains its author and exact target version; opening it from Activity or a goal does not create a second conversation.

Discussion can continue without taking control

Anyone in the permitted audience can comment asynchronously. A comment contributes to the discussion without automatically changing a goal or acknowledged brief. Private conversations remain outside the project unless an owner deliberately releases an excerpt. Activity summarizes what changed and links back to the discussion.

Two viewpoints, one shared objective

Switch the guide’s simulated actor to see Davide in Build while Luis inspects Explore. Each retains a local lens, selected object and draft. Follow shared focus and Follow this build are separate preferences; neither grants access or changes B1.

An owner action belongs to its owner

A request for Luis’s development connection is visible to the permitted team, but only Luis can complete the simulated owner step. Davide can inspect the reason and ask Luis. Passing guide control cannot authorize the account or transfer the final product decision.

Visible completion: Guide transfer remains visible in both viewpoints while local lenses differ, Luis retains his account action and Davide retains final acceptance.

Implementation in progressW1 · B1 · first layout available · interaction checks continue
Ready when calledTeam Sophia · Meaningful decisions

Preserve cooperation cards, participation preferences, decisions, task organization and the goal view. Cross-lens bridges refer to the same work records; amendments progress through recorded, provider-accepted, observed and checked stages.

Keep what already works

  • The compact dock, Updates filters, contextual actions, and Undo.
  • The choice to stay close or let implementation continue.

Review the useful part

A coherent partial preview creates one useful review opportunity linked to its exact source. The same item in Activity opens the same context. Optional review does not stop unrelated eligible work. Required obligations remain reachable even when a viewer dismisses a suggestion.

Clarification is different from a new brief

Keep the compatible style-change and larger follow-up actions. The compatible change becomes A1 against its source and effective brief revision: recorded, provider accepted, incorporation observed, then checked. Mobile onboarding remains a separate follow-up. Neither quietly replaces the active candidate or mutates frozen B1.

Resolve the choice, then the card

Moving a decision to Done asks for its actual answer and records who chose it. The board, project snapshot and Activity agree. B1 stays immutable: a later decision is an attributed record or explicit amendment, not an invisible rewrite of the dispatched packet. Ordinary human task organization keeps its reversible Move and Undo actions.

Explain participation concretely

A preference change receives a useful acknowledgment: I’ll bring you the next useful preview; implementation will continue. An unsupported provider change is explained rather than presented as applied.

Give the outcome a durable home

Add Goals as a first-class project view. A goal owns the desired outcome and agreed success criteria; linked work records the commitments; execution attempts record how particular providers pursued them. Show these relations together with discussions, decisions, evidence, and the next unresolved issue. A failed attempt or provider switch does not erase the goal.

Show evidence, not an invented percentage

Keep goal state separate from runner state and dependency-specific waiting. Show satisfied, failing and unverified criteria. A provider turn or returned file is not achievement. A candidate requires its applicable checks and the agreed acceptance policy; small edits may remain ordinary tasks without a goal.

Request here, open the result when useful

“Build the selected direction” can be admitted from Converse while the person stays in Converse; a compact bridge opens the exact Build object. “Build it and show me” navigates explicitly. Routine progress updates that existing object instead of adding a fresh interruption each time.

A request and an amendment are different inputs

H1 may need Luis while Davide discusses a design change. Record A1 separately; it does not answer the account request. Required work controls and owner obligations remain persistent, while one discretionary review or suggestion is prominent at a time. Stop retains priority over both.

Visible completion: The same request, contribution, decision and amendment agree across their views. Dismissing a card changes attention; it neither answers a question nor rewrites B1.

Keep the inspectable brief, goal-or-task choice, autonomous repair and returned-result comparison. Extend B1 with exact source, assets, behavior, integration gaps, repository fit, authority and checks; retain it unchanged after dispatch.

Keep what already works

  • One Sophia presence remains available throughout delegated work.
  • Repository detail appears where it helps a meaningful choice.

A brief that can be inspected

Inspect B1 in three areas: Brief and boundaries; Included context and integration map; Checks, execution and return. It carries the exact selected frontend source, component locations, tokens, approved assets, scenarios, run instructions, repository base, exclusions, owner and expected evidence. Its bytes freeze at dispatch.

The account still belongs to its owner

Keep owner-specific executor selection and Ready / Offline examples. Luis and Davide’s routes are capability fixtures, not promises about every Codex or Claude Code installation. Show which owner, environment and integration mode actually holds this attempt; no pooled subscription, credential collection or live dispatch is implied.

Make the value of review visible

Candidate C1 deliberately fails a named requirement. Keep the last stable prototype available, inspect C1 and let the permitted repair return C2 with corrected evidence against the same criteria. Davide accepts exact C2 under the demonstrated policy. Acceptance changes no export, merge or publication permission.

Authorize pursuit of the goal

For substantial work, authorize implementation, inspection, testing and bounded repair under the project goal. Retain the single-task option. Ordinary comments leave the mandate unchanged; a clear permitted correction creates A1 with separate delivery and evidence stages. Only the owning implementation path writes the candidate.

Supervise meaningful boundaries

The coding harness owns its internal iteration. Sophia checks meaningful progress, missing decisions, budget limits, stalled attempts, and returned evidence. Co-review can help during execution without making every edit or test a human gate. A mechanically verified criterion and a product-taste decision may use different acceptance rules.

Borrow lifecycle machinery with clear ownership

DeepSeek’s goal mechanisms offer revisioned goal states and separately controlled continuation. Sophia should adapt those primitives to project goals spanning people, conversations, and providers. Continuation permission is distinct from saved goal state, and marking a provider run complete is not evidence that the project goal has been achieved.

Readiness is different from receipt

A missing mandatory source or contract keeps B1 incomplete and blocks dispatch with a specific repair. Optional omitted context remains disclosed. Admitted, provider accepted and intake complete are separate states; a stack mismatch produces an explicit integration issue rather than a reassuring success label.

Resolve the exact development connection

H1 names Luis, W1 and its affected database verification. The owner opens a clearly simulated flow and reports completion. Verification of the exact development connection is a separate event, followed by requested and confirmed continuation. A reported login alone cannot display verified access.

Inspect what actually travels and returns

Preview remains central. Compare and Inspect reveal the relevant source, changes, asset versions, applicable B1/A1 and checks. The integration map identifies each mock, its intended service replacement and the proof required. A source change alone does not establish correct authentication, durability or collaboration.

Control follows the route’s capabilities

Compare active-turn input, next-boundary delivery, controlled interruption and unknown delivery. These fixtures use different wording and actions. Preserve an unconfirmed amendment without blind replay, and keep provider acceptance, observed incorporation and checked result separate.

Visible completion: Missing required source prevents dispatch. H1 is resolved by its owner through separate evidence stages; a failed check is repaired before Davide accepts exact C2 without merge or publication.

Retain project snapshots, per-work packets, exact excerpt release, memory semantics, offline recovery and Stop settlement. Add current owner requests, correlated native resolution, stale observations and late-response handling.

Keep what already works

  • Group control over shared memory and explicit private releases.
  • Personal journals and rituals stay in their proper scope.

Maintain a current brief

Show the goal, accepted direction, artifacts, unanswered questions, dissent, and outstanding work. An accepted project fact is usable immediately; it does not need a separate reusable-lesson experiment.

Release exactly what is shown

Preview one neutral synthetic private design excerpt, its version, and its audience. Cancel changes nothing. Share adds only that excerpt to the project; private source material remains private.

Recovery starts with confirmed facts

When Luis’s runner disconnects, show Waiting for Luis’s computer and the last confirmed step. Reconnect restores W1 without a second dispatch. A Stop request remains Stopping until settled; unknown outcomes stay explicitly unresolved.

Precise memory language

Use Not used — restore to make available again for retained but excluded material. Say These memory suggestions will not be used until reviewed for candidates. Neither phrase means that authorized project records disappeared.

An unresolved request survives the interface

H1 remains the same request after a lens change, modal close, chapter visit, local refresh or return. Its owner, target and current status matter more than its unread badge. Native-tool resolution updates this same record; stale or reused answers cannot satisfy a changed request.

Connection loss has different meanings

A disconnected UI can differ from an unavailable local executor or stale observation of a remote run. State only what is known. If Stop has ended authorization, a later verified account callback cannot restart the task; a new permitted continuation is required.

Private release does not rewrite past work

Keep the exact excerpt preview, owner check, version and project audience. A later release becomes eligible for subsequent context selection but never retroactively enters frozen B1. Local browser restoration here is a convenience for this demonstration, not proof of production durability.

Visible completion: Return shows the same accepted version, follow-up, unresolved H1 and last known work state; a late authorization cannot revive stopped work.

DonorUser benefitBoundary

Sophia owns cross-person project goals, authority, continuation and evidence-based acceptance; this HTML makes no new upstream claim.
